extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers / wartime news consumers
extracted.subtask_description: Reporting and filing front-line wartime newspaper dispatches that summarize military operations, damage, losses and official statements; often subject to censorship and reliant on official or first‑hand sources. Emphasizes geographic specificity, force counts, and attribution to governments or radio/airmen reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Censorship / delay for security
rubrics_metrics.description: (This dispatch apparently wa delayed by censorship Ay')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wartime dispatches may be delayed or censored for security reasons; reporters and editors should note and, where appropriate, indicate that reports were held or redacted by censors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution to official communiqués and headquarters
rubrics_metrics.description: Allied headquarters said...; It was announced officially that...; The American States Strategic Air Forces said...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on and cite official statements (Allied headquarters, strategic air forces, Moscow broadcasts, etc.) for authoritative facts; clearly attribute claims to the issuing agency or government rather than presenting them as independent confirmed fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of air photographs as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Air photographs showed that at least three direct hits were scored on the Brest-sub pens, penetrating the structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When available, incorporate and cite aerial photographic evidence to support strike/target claims; specify what the photographs showed (hits, penetrations, damage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantification of forces, sorties and losses
rubrics_metrics.description: Formations of more than 1,400 American and British heavy bombers... more than 1,100 American Flying Fortresses and Liberators... Thirteen American heavy bombers and six fighters were lost.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise numbers and types (sorties, bombers, fighters, losses) where possible to convey scale; when figures come from official sources or estimates, attribute them accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic and target specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Attacking numerous targets in Dollbergen, Hannover... Brest... Pas de Calais... oil refinery at Dollbergen, an oil storage plant at Nienburg, an aircraft parts factory and freight yard at Fallersleben...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List specific locations and targets (cities, facilities, ports, bridges) to situate actions and impacts; specify regions and transport/communication lines threatened or hit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of first‑hand/returning airmen reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Returning airmen reported the Germans sent up rocket-propelled planes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include eyewitness or participant reports (returning airmen, pilots) for operational details, but attribute such anecdotal accounts and reconcile them with other evidence where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of enemy-source reports and radio claims
rubrics_metrics.description: The German radio said fierce air combats developed and claimed... The Frankfort radio went off the air near midnight, indicating the RAF was over the Continent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report and attribute claims made by enemy radio or press, noting their source and potential bias; use them as context rather than unquestioned fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain operational intent and tactical objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: The mission was designed to trap the enemy submarines in their pens and block the seaward escape of any high German officers cut off in Brittany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When possible, describe the intended tactical or operational purpose of missions (e.g., trapping submarines, hitting launch sites) to give readers context for the strikes and targets.
